warnings: Scope of US-002 partially out of this code unit: rule 06 / FAIRNESS-GATE also require (1) per-segment ACCURACY alongside FPR, (2) the dataset's demographic-distribution validator (T-002-b, data-redteam, rule 03), and (3) human-review/contestation escalation for rejections. fairness.py correctly delivers the PRIMARY disaggregated-FPR + significance contract (T-002-a); the remaining gate items are separate deliverables and are NOT certified here.

audit_parity tests each segment vs the pooled rest. With >2 segments and no multiple-comparison correction, family-wise alpha inflates slightly. Not a defect for the US-002 contract (alpha is an explicit parameter and BLOCK on any disparity is conservative/fail-safe), but a future hardening note.

fpr()/disaggregated_fpr() return 0.0 FPR for an empty segment (n_legit=0); two_proportion_p returns 1.0 (non-significant) for empty groups. A segment with zero legit samples would be silently treated as parity-OK. Acceptable given rule-03 dataset validation is a prerequisite, but worth surfacing.
